subject: Chat stream heartbeat failures causing 5xx/429 spike - urgent

Subject: Production: Chat stream failures, 429 spike and reconnect storms

Hi Logan,

We're seeing a large uptick in 429s and intermittent 5xx responses from the chat streaming endpoint since ~14:50 PT. Symptoms: many of our clients report idle stream disconnects, then aggressive client-side retries (no backoff) which seem to cause a retry storm and a sustained elevated 429 rate for the last 20–30 minutes.

Impact: roughly 18% of active sessions experienced a dropped stream and automated retry loops; product teams are getting paged. We've attached a short trace (connect-trace-20260609.log) and RPS metrics showing the spike.

Can you confirm whether this is an issue on your side (gateway idle timeouts, keepalive) or something in our integration? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an exec contact.

Example request ids: req_9f7a2c, req_9f7a3e, req_9f7b01 (included in the log).

- We'll temporarily enable a smoothing policy to limit per-connection reconnect bursts and apply server-side exponential backoff for connections we detect as retry storms.

I'll keep you posted every ~30 minutes. I'm copying Karthik for any decisions on a dedicated pool / SLA credit. If you want an exec call, we can join now.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: Chat stream failures, 429 spike and reconnect storms

FYI — initial triage notes: we've correlated the 429 spike with a pattern of idle stream disconnects where the idle timeout handshake (gateway -> worker) races with client reconnects. Observations:

- At 14:48 PT a subset of edge gateways started dropping TCP keepalives (environmental flapping) leading to idle stream closure.
- Clients without exponential backoff aggressively re-open and re-authenticate, increasing short-lived session creation and KV-cache churn. This increases per-request latency and leads to 429s from our rate-limiter.
- Error signatures match the request ids Alex attached.

Immediate mitigations (implemented 15:30 PT):
1) Increased gateway idle timeout from 60s -> 120s to reduce false idle disconnects.
2) Enabled server-side reconnection-smoothing: enforce a short randomized jitter and reject high-frequency reconnects with 429+Retry-After header instead of allowing unbounded retries.
3) Pushed a temporary knob for higher per-customer token bucket for MediCore to absorb increased short-term load.

Next actions (ETA):
- 60m: confirm reduction in 429 rate via rps-metrics-20260609.csv delta.
- 3h: roll a keepalive/heartbeat probe for long-lived streams (client/server ping) in dedicated routing path for MediCore.
- 24h: propose config to route MediCore to a dedicated pool during business hours if they agree (to eliminate noisy-neighbor effects).

I'll monitor. Attaching a short mitigation plan: incident-mitigation-plan.pdf

Grace
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
From: Alex Morris <alex.morris@medicore.ai>

Thanks Logan and Grace — appreciate the rapid action. We've seen the endpoints stabilize after the gateway timeout bump and the smoothing policy. Metrics show a drop from ~18% failed sessions to ~3% failed sessions in the last 40m.

A couple items:
- We will push a client patch to include exponential backoff and jitter; ETA 48 hours.
- We need an exec-level note for our leadership and a short timeline for the dedicated pool option. Also if possible please surface any provisional credit for hours of degraded availability (we'll reference the attached RPS CSV and our internal incident report).

I've attached a small sampling of client logs where the client retried without backoff (connect-trace-20260609.log).

If you can provide a 1-page executive summary and a proposed credit amount, I will route to our procurement and legal.

--
Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec note: MediCore incident summary + recommended remedies

Marcus — quick summary for visibility and sign-off:

What happened: Gateway keepalive flapping caused idle stream disconnects which triggered aggressive client reconnects from the MediCore SDK. The reconnect pattern caused a retry storm, KV-cache churn, and a transient 429/5xx escalation during a 20–30 minute window on 2026-06-09.

What we did:
- Raised gateway idle timeout + enabled per-connection smoothing (immediate).
- Applied temporary elevated token-bucket for MediCore to reduce user-facing 429s.
- Plan: Add a heartbeat channel and routing to a dedicated pool for MediCore during peak hours (requires approval for capacity reserve).

Customer impact: Short-term degraded availability for a subset of sessions; currently stabilized to ~3% failed sessions.

Recommendation / asks:
- Approve one-time SLA credit (proposed: 10% invoice credit for impacted billing window) and a dedicated pool pilot for 30 days.
- Authorize systems team to add a permanent keepalive probe and to roll client guidance in the SDK docs (we will provide guidance for exponential backoff patterns).

Attachments: incident-mitigation-plan.pdf, rps-metrics-20260609.csv

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
